methodology: Both the original research topic and the generated technical specification were decomposed into atomic units by identifying individual requirements, features, behaviors, and constraints. Each atomic unit was designed to be independent, self-contained, technically specific, unambiguous, and implementable as a single requirement. This involved breaking down complex sentences into simpler, more manageable statements. For the original research topic, the decomposition focused on the game rules, grid properties, input/output signals, and operational behavior. For the generated technical specification, the decomposition focused on the combinational logic functions, loading logic, game of life update logic, neighbor counting, state update rules, and grid representation.
mindtraced_atomic_units: Game of Life implemented on a 16x16 toroidal grid
Cell (x, y) stored at index (y * 16 + x) of 'q'
Grid wraps around on both axes (toroidal topology)
Game state updates every clock cycle
Living cell with 2 or 3 neighbors lives
Dead cell with exactly 3 neighbors becomes alive (reproduction)
'load' input high loads 'data' into 'q' at next clock edge
'load' input low updates game state every clock cycle
module top_module(input clk, input load, input [255:0] data, output reg [255:0] q);
spec_atomic_units: Implements Conway's Game of Life on a 16x16 toroidal grid
'clk' input is not relevant for combinational logic specification
'load' asserted loads 'data' into 'q'
'load' deasserted, 'q' reflects next state based on game rules
'data' input provides initial state of 16x16 grid
'q' output represents current state of the game
q = load ? data : next_state;
Neighbor Counting: Count live neighbors for each cell (row, col)
Toroidal grid: neighbors are (row-1, col-1), (row-1, col), (row-1, col+1), (row, col-1), (row, col+1), (row+1, col-1), (row+1, col), (row+1, col+1)
row and col are taken modulo 16 for toroidal boundary conditions
If cell is alive and neighbor count < 2 or > 3, cell dies
If cell is alive and neighbor count is 2 or 3, cell remains alive
If cell is dead and neighbor count is exactly 3, cell becomes alive
Otherwise, the cell remains dead
next_state[row*16 + col] = (q[row*16 + col] && (neighbor_count == 2 || neighbor_count == 3)) || (!q[row*16 + col] && (neighbor_count == 3));
Toroidal Neighbor Calculation: (row - 1 + 16) % 16, (col - 1 + 16) % 16 etc.
Neighbor Counting Logic: Sum states of neighbors
State Update Logic: next_state[row*16 + col] = (q[row*16 + col] & ((neighbor_count == 2) | (neighbor_count == 3))) | (!q[row*16 + col] & (neighbor_count == 3));
Loading Logic: q = load ? data : next_state;
Grid Representation: q[15:0] represents row 0, q[31:16] represents row 1, etc.
